title: WD drive not detected by computer
shortDescription: The external drive doesn't appear in File Explorer or Finder.
fullDescription:
A WD My Book or My Passport that doesn't show up typically has a USB/power problem or a corrupted partition table. The LED may be solid, blinking, or off depending on cause.

Data loss is possible – do not initialize or format the drive without first attempting recovery.
symptoms: LED on but no drive letter

fixSteps.title: Try different cable and port
fixSteps.instruction: Use the original WD cable directly into a rear USB port (not a hub). For My Book, verify power adapter is connected.

fixSteps.title: Check Disk Management
fixSteps.instruction: Open Disk Management (Windows) or Disk Utility (Mac). If the drive shows as 'Unknown' or 'Not Initialized', do NOT initialize – this erases the partition table.

fixSteps.title: Run WD Drive Utilities SMART
fixSteps.instruction: Install WD Drive Utilities and run SMART diagnostic before any recovery attempts.

whenToCallPro: Critical data on the drive: use a professional data recovery service before any fix attempts.

faq.a: No – this erases the partition table and risks data loss. Investigate first.

title: I/O error reading or writing WD drive
shortDescription: Reads or writes fail with I/O error messages.
fullDescription: I/O errors on a WD drive indicate the OS cannot reliably read or write sectors. This can be cable, controller, or failing media. Data may be at risk – copy what you can immediately.
symptoms: 'The request failed due to a fatal device hardware error'

fixSteps.title: Copy data now
fixSteps.instruction: Back up any accessible data to another drive before troubleshooting further.

fixSteps.title: SMART check
fixSteps.instruction: Run WD Drive Utilities > Diagnose > Quick Drive Test and SMART status.

fixSteps.title: CHKDSK / First Aid
fixSteps.instruction: Windows: chkdsk X: /f. Mac: Disk Utility First Aid. Only if SMART is passing.

whenToCallPro: If clicking, beeping, or rapid sector loss – stop and call a data recovery service.
videoSearchQuery: WD external drive I/O error fix

faq.a: Only on drives passing SMART – on failing drives chkdsk can accelerate damage.

title: WD drive reporting imminent SMART failure
shortDescription: SMART indicates the drive is close to failure.
fullDescription:
SMART failure warnings mean attributes like reallocated sectors, pending sectors, or seek errors have exceeded thresholds. Drive should be considered failing – back up immediately.

Do not run intensive write tests; stick to reads.

fixSteps.title: Immediate backup
fixSteps.instruction: Copy critical files to another drive before the SMART situation worsens.

fixSteps.title: Replace drive
fixSteps.instruction: SMART-failing drives cannot be reliably repaired – plan replacement.

fixSteps.title: Return under warranty
fixSteps.instruction: Use WD warranty status portal to RMA if in-warranty.

whenToCallPro: If data is critical and the drive is too degraded to finish a full backup, consult a recovery pro.

faq.q: Can I keep using a SMART-failing drive?
faq.a: Not safely – back up and replace.

title: WD drive stuck in read-only mode
fullDescription: Write protection on a WD external drive is usually caused by filesystem errors, NTFS 'dirty bit', or the drive entering a fail-safe read-only state after detecting issues.

fixSteps.title: Check dirty bit (Windows)
fixSteps.instruction: Run 'fsutil dirty query X:'. If dirty, run chkdsk X: /f to clear.

fixSteps.title: Check SMART
fixSteps.instruction: If drive went read-only as self-protection, SMART likely shows failures.

fixSteps.title: Mac NTFS write
fixSteps.instruction: Install NTFS-3G or similar driver if using on macOS.

whenToCallPro: If drive self-locks to read-only due to SMART, call data recovery.

faq.a: Usually yes if caused by a dirty bit; not if the drive is self-protecting.

title: My Passport spinning up and down on USB
shortDescription: Drive repeatedly powers up/down due to low USB power.
fullDescription: Bus-powered WD drives need a full 900 mA USB 3.0 port. Front-panel ports, hubs without external power, or long cables may under-supply current.

fixSteps.title: Rear motherboard port
fixSteps.instruction: Plug directly into rear USB 3.0/3.1 port.

fixSteps.title: Short OEM cable
fixSteps.instruction: Use the short cable shipped with the drive.

fixSteps.title: Y-cable or powered hub
fixSteps.instruction: For older laptops, use a dual-head Y-cable or powered hub.

videoSearchQuery: WD My Passport USB power fix

faq.a: Yes, modern USB-C ports deliver more current and are usually sufficient.

title: You need to format the disk before you can use it
shortDescription: Windows prompts to format an otherwise good drive.
fullDescription: This prompt appears when the partition table is damaged, encryption keys are unavailable, or filesystem metadata is corrupt. Do NOT format if your data matters – format is destructive.
symptoms: Drive shows as RAW in Disk Management

fixSteps.title: Do not format
fixSteps.instruction: Cancel any format dialog to preserve data.

fixSteps.title: Unlock if encrypted
fixSteps.instruction: If WD Security was enabled, open WD Drive Utilities and unlock with password.

fixSteps.title: Run recovery software
fixSteps.instruction: Use TestDisk or WD Data Recovery service to rebuild partition.

whenToCallPro: Data recovery service for critical data – DIY fix may fail and worsen damage.

faq.a: It recovers usability but erases all data.

title: File corruption on WD external drive
shortDescription: Files open with errors, CRC failures, or mismatched sizes.
fullDescription: Corruption on WD drives appears as CRC errors, zero-byte files, or unexpected file system damage. Could be bad sectors, power loss during write, or cable issues.

causes.cause: Unsafe ejection / power loss during write

fixSteps.title: Back up healthy files
fixSteps.instruction: Before repair, copy what opens to another drive.

fixSteps.title: Run chkdsk/First Aid
fixSteps.instruction: chkdsk X: /f on Windows, Disk Utility First Aid on Mac.

fixSteps.title: SMART surface check
fixSteps.instruction: If SMART fails, plan replacement – corruption will return.

whenToCallPro: Clicking sounds, rapid sector growth – call pro.

faq.a: Yes – prevents write corruption especially on Windows.

title: File system on WD drive damaged or RAW
shortDescription: Drive shown as RAW or damaged by OS.
fullDescription: The partition exists but filesystem structures (MFT/catalog) are corrupt. Files are inaccessible until repaired with a filesystem tool or rescued with recovery software.
symptoms: Drive shows RAW in Disk Management

fixSteps.title: Image first
fixSteps.instruction: Make a sector-by-sector image (ddrescue) before repair attempts.

fixSteps.title: Run TestDisk
fixSteps.instruction: Use TestDisk to rebuild partition table and boot sector.

fixSteps.title: Recover files
fixSteps.instruction: PhotoRec or R-Studio against the image to extract files.

whenToCallPro: Critical data – go straight to a data recovery service.
videoSearchQuery: WD drive RAW file system fix

faq.a: No – files often recoverable but do not format.

title: WD drive transfers much slower than expected
shortDescription: Transfers capped at USB 2.0 speeds or lower.
fullDescription: A USB 3.0 WD drive connected via a USB 2.0 cable or port falls to ~35 MB/s. Enabled WD Security encryption also adds minor overhead on older drives.

fixSteps.title: Use USB 3.0 port
fixSteps.instruction: Plug into blue/teal or USB-C port labeled SS.

fixSteps.title: Genuine USB 3.0 cable
fixSteps.instruction: Use OEM cable; avoid cheap knockoffs.

fixSteps.title: Archive small files
fixSteps.instruction: Zip/tar groups of small files before transferring.

videoSearchQuery: WD external drive slow transfer fix

faq.q: Why so slow with small files?
faq.a: Per-file overhead dominates; archiving reduces it.

title: WD drive locked by WD Security
shortDescription: Drive mounts as virtual CD requiring password unlock.
fullDescription: Drives with WD Security enabled boot into a locked mode showing only a virtual CD with the unlock utility. Without the password, data is effectively unrecoverable due to hardware AES.

fixSteps.title: Install WD Security
fixSteps.instruction: Download latest WD Security / WD Drive Utilities.

fixSteps.title: Enter password
fixSteps.instruction: Unlock drive, check 'Remember' for auto-unlock on that PC.

fixSteps.title: Reset (data loss)
fixSteps.instruction: If password lost, WD Drive Utilities can factory-reset the drive – erases all data.

whenToCallPro: Professional recovery rarely helps with hardware AES – data is typically unrecoverable without password.

faq.a: No – WD cannot recover or bypass the encryption password.

title: WD drive clicking or beeping
fullDescription: Clicking/beeping indicates head or spindle mechanical problems. The drive is failing – stop using it and contact a data recovery specialist immediately. Every power-on may worsen the situation.

fixSteps.title: Power off immediately
fixSteps.instruction: Do not keep powering up a clicking drive.

fixSteps.title: Try Y-cable (beeping only)
fixSteps.instruction: For beeping from low power, Y-cable or powered hub may help.

fixSteps.title: Data recovery service
fixSteps.instruction: For clicking, contact a certified cleanroom data recovery service.

faq.a: Never – heads require a cleanroom to service.

title: MyCloud setup error
fullDescription: Initial setup did not complete. Common diagnostic indication on Western Digital external drive. Most issues resolve with reset, firmware update, or hardware swap.

fixSteps.title: Update firmware
fixSteps.instruction: Check for and install latest firmware via app or web UI.

fixSteps.title: Factory reset if needed
fixSteps.instruction: If error persists, factory-reset and reconfigure.

whenToCallPro: If reset and firmware update don't resolve, contact support.

faq.a: Often yes — power-cycling resolves transient errors.
Yes, but don't interrupt power during update.
